jobs.title: Director Enterprise Applications, Data
jobs.description:
Director, Application, Data & Integration | Dynamics 365 · AI-Assisted Engineering (Claude Code) ·

Downtown Vancouver (Hybrid)

TEEMA Group is partnering with a well-established, growing Vancouver-based professional services firm
to hire a Director, Application, Data & Integration
. It’s a rare chance for an engineering-minded technology leader to build modern application, data and integration capabilities from the ground up and shape the future of technology across the firm.

The opportunity

You’ll build and lead the firm’s enterprise application, data and integration capabilities. A key part of the mandate is transforming how the development team works through AI-assisted engineering, automation and modern DevOps
, delivering major gains in productivity and delivery speed. You’ll also build the firm’s data engineering and analytics capability and own the integration architecture that connects its core systems, as part of a broader technology modernization strategy.

The ideal candidate

Comes from a software engineering background.
You’ve written production code and still think like an engineer, not just a manager of engineers.
Has real Dynamics 365 experience
, ideally leading or architecting implementations, integrations or extensions on the Dynamics and Power Platform.
Uses AI coding tools hands-on
, such as Claude Code
, GitHub Copilot or similar, and has used them to measurably speed up development, testing and documentation for a team.

What you’ll do

Application strategy and architecture:
lead technical direction across the application landscape, set architecture and lifecycle standards, guide solution design, and oversee implementation partners.
Engineering discipline, DevOps and AI:
mature development standards, source control, code review and testing; establish CI/CD and release management; embed secure development; and lead adoption of AI-assisted development across the team.
Integration architecture:
own integration standards and approaches for APIs and system-to-system data exchange, making sure integrations are secure, resilient and well monitored.
Dynamics 365 leadership:
provide technical leadership for a major Dynamics 365 transition, working with product owners and implementation partners, and build internal capability to support and extend the platform.
Data and analytics:
develop the enterprise data architecture, build data engineering capabilities, and set approaches for master data, data quality and lineage so the firm has consistent, trusted reporting.
People leadership:
build and lead a multidisciplinary team spanning development, integration, QA, data engineering and analytics, balancing internal staff, partners and specialized contractors.
Security and operations:
partner with IT Operations to build security, resilience and data protection into everything the team delivers.

What you bring

Progressive technology leadership across enterprise applications, software engineering, integration and data
A track record of building or maturing software engineering and DevOps practices (CI/CD, automated testing, secure development, application lifecycle management)
Strong knowledge of modern application architecture, APIs, integrations and cloud platforms
Experience in data architecture, data engineering, analytics or BI
Experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams and external technology partners
Excellent communication skills with both technical teams and business leaders

You’ll thrive here if you are:
a builder who’s comfortable creating capabilities that don’t yet exist, disciplined about engineering but pragmatic about delivery, and forward-looking on how AI and automation can change the way technology is delivered.

Work arrangement:
hybrid, with 3 days a week in the downtown Vancouver office and 2 days from home
(hybrid begins after the probationary period).

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
About Toptal

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe
, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Position Description:

As Chief Technology Officer, you will drive execution for the product and engineering teams and put AI at the core of everything the company builds. You will own Toptal’s full technical architecture and you will build it AI-first—utilizing best practices for agentic engineering. AI is not a workstream inside the engineering team—it’s core to it.

You will create and own the AI architecture and best practices the rest of the company utilizes. You will also own the initiatives that put agents into production. You should know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up, how to engineer best-in-class harnesses, and how to create best practices for agentic engineering that engineering teams adopt to 10x their productivity—without sacrificing quality. Your mindset will be that of a builder and an architect, someone who solves problems in the system itself. No problem will be too large or too small for you to solve yourself. You will set the technical direction and hold the cadenced meetings that turn technical strategy into working, production-ready outcomes. You will be in the design reviews and in the code, not adjacent to them. You will move fast, and you will ensure our engineering team is never the reason an initiative slows down.

You are the technical owner of all Toptal’s products. You will collaborate closely with Product to design infrastructure that exposes Toptal’s core business logic through modular interfaces the rest of the business can build on. Alongside a group of hands-on executives, your engineering discipline directly shapes Toptal’s growth, profitability, and operational excellence.

You will own resourcing and workforce planning as a doer: scoping the work, sizing the teams, planning headcount against it, defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing them off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about hiring A-players—with a sense of urgency.

Then, you lead the team. You will set the standards, develop people against those standards, and know exactly who is meeting those standards.

You will be one of Toptal’s foremost experts on AI, and you will stay ahead of a field that never stops moving. You will coach engineers on agentic best practices, show the executive team what is newly possible with the new AI tooling, and push AI into every function at Toptal.

This role runs on high-energy execution and attention to detail. You will bring urgency to every part of it and measure yourself on outcomes. We are not looking for someone to oversee this work. We are looking for someone to drive it and get into the details.

This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.

One precondition runs through all of it: you conceive the strategy. You will form your own view of where engineering and AI should go, build the case, and bring the CEO a strategy to react to, not a request for direction.

AI and agentic engineering

Own Toptal’s AI technology strategy and the architecture beneath it: model selection and fine-tuning, harness design, orchestration, retrieval, context engineering, tool and MCP integration, guardrails, evaluation, and cost control, exposed as primitives every team composes against.
Deploy agentic engineering at scale against the work that runs this business: matching, vetting, onboarding, delivery, and internal operations. Own the outcomes those agents are accountable for.
Make AI quality measurable. Own the evals, the regression suites, and the review loops, so quality here is proven rather than claimed.
Rebuild how the platform gets built and operated, raising output per engineer through AI-assisted development, review, testing, and operations. Engineers have to want this, not comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.

Team, resourcing, and accountability

Decide what a team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.
Own resourcing and workforce planning: scope the roadmap into buildable work, plan headcount and sequence, write the specs, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.
Own the bar for the team: assess talent honestly, develop people against the bar, and hold it as the organization grows.

Platform and execution

Own the architecture end-to-end, from services and data flows to interfaces and system boundaries, and hold the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.
Own throughput, reliability, and the platform layer beneath them, including the AI-dependent paths where latency, drift, and provider outages are real failure modes. Own build-versus-buy, technical debt, secure-by-design architecture, responsible AI, and the engineering and AI cost structure down to inference and token spend.

In the first week, expect to:

Learn Toptal’s model and platform architecture, and meet the leaders you will depend on across Engineering, Product, Industries, and Services.
Establish a direct, working rhythm with the CEO.

In the first month, expect to:

Assess the engineering function honestly, and assess AI maturity with it: what is really in production, what is measured, what is duplicated, and what should be shut down.
Assess the team against the bar this role requires, and bring the executive team a strategy no one asked you for.

In the first three months, expect to:

Be executing your own plan, with a review cadence and clear accountability at every level, and your resourcing plan presented.
Stand up the shared AI architecture and evals, and put one agentic workflow into production with a baseline and a measured result.

In the first six months, expect to:

Show business impact from agents in production in at least two core workflows, with the evidence behind it.
Have the leadership team you need, with the bar visibly raised, and throughput and reliability moving on the paths that matter most.

In the first year, expect to:

Run an engineering organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with the pull on AI now coming from engineering.
Have AI leverage embedded in the architecture and the operating model, not living in a portfolio of pilots, and the team you built delivering against plan.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field is required, and an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
15+ years of progressive engineering leadership, including significant time as a CTO or VP of Engineering, or as a direct report to one at meaningful scale.
Deep, current, hands-on command of modern AI engineering: foundation models, agentic architectures, harness design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation. You have shipped and operated these in production, and you know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up.
Agentic systems deployed at scale against real business processes, with measured outcomes on cost, cycle time, quality, or revenue, and a record of retiring what did not work.
Rigor about evaluation. You can explain precisely how you knew a model, prompt, or agent change was an improvement, and you can show the evidence.
Command of the economics underneath it: model routing, hosted versus self-hosted, inference capacity, latency and cost budgets, and staying portable across providers.
Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.
You create strategy rather than administer it, and you win arguments on evidence rather than authority, including your view on what a team should look like in the age of AI.
Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, and a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.
Currently hands-on. You read and write code, you can take apart a design document or an eval harness and find the flaw in it, and you command distributed systems, service architecture, data-intensive applications, and cloud infrastructure at scale.
Experience scaling and modernizing a large existing codebase without stopping the business. You have replaced load-bearing systems in flight, not only built greenfield.
Experience leading a globally distributed, remote team at a technology or hyper-growth company is required. A high-volume, two-sided marketplace or multi-tenant platform is a significant plus.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
Speed, ownership, and quality. You move with urgency, decide without perfect information, and treat everything you deliver as a reflection of yourself.
You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

jobs.title: Director, Product Automation
jobs.description:
Job Description:

ICUC is the global leader in Social Media solutions for over 20 years. To date, the ICUC team consists of over 350 people, in over 35 countries, covering 50 languages around the clock. In an environment where the only constant is change, we create common ground between brands and audiences across communities and social media. Fueled by a unique culture built in and around meritocracy, we bring the passion, the know-how and the balance necessary to maintain the charted course we set for ourselves: to be the best, we employ the best. Are you ready to be part of the ICUC team?

The Role

ICUC is creating a new leadership role to own our automation and AI strategy across the business. This is a product and innovation mandate, not a workforce-efficiency one: the Director, Product Automation is responsible for how AI and automation get built into the actual work we do for clients — community management, strategy, insights, monitoring, and social listening, so our teams can work faster, with more precision, and with sharper focus on the client.

This is a founding, leadership-level position. You'll set the vision and build the function from the ground up, working closely across leadership to make sure ICUC's AI and automation strategy is as strong internally as it is in how we tell that story to the market.

What You'll Be Doing

Automation & AI Strategy

Own ICUC's automation and AI strategy as it applies to our products and service delivery
Evaluate, pilot, and select tools and technologies that make our core services - community management, strategy, insights, monitoring, and social listening - faster, more precise, and more scalable, without compromising the quality clients expect.
Define a standardized, scalable automation blueprint for ICUC's service offerings, rather than one-off, client-by-client fixes.
Build the reporting infrastructure needed to measure automation impact including efficiency gains, quality, and margin — across our platform ecosystem.
Bring a product mindset to this work: treat automation and AI capability as a product to be designed, tested, and iterated, not a back-office project.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Partner closely with Operations, Product Marketing and Growth to translate our internal automation and AI capability into external go-to-market positioning and messaging.
Collaborate with Marketing to align messaging with ICUC's broader brand and content strategy.
Work across delivery, operations, and client success teams to ensure new tools and workflows are adopted in practice, not just approved in theory.

Organizational Leadership

Represent automation and AI strategy at the leadership table, helping shape how ICUC positions itself against AI-native competitors and evolving client expectations.
Build and champion a clear, company-wide narrative for what "AI-enabled, human-powered" means at ICUC, internally and externally.
Mentor and influence teams across the business to build automation literacy and confidence, without a large direct team of your own at the outset.

What You Bring To The Table

Proven experience building or scaling a product, automation, or AI/technology strategy function, ideally within a services, agency, or martech environment.
A track record of taking automation or AI capability from concept to measurable operational impact.
Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; comfortable partnering with marketing, delivery, and executive stakeholders who may have different priorities.
Familiarity with social media, community management, or social listening platforms is a strong asset.
Experience navigating the reporting and data limitations of enterprise martech platforms and building workarounds or systems to close those gaps.
A genuine product-innovation mindset: curious about tools and technology but always tying it back to what makes the client experience better.
Comfortable operating as a founding leader in a new function - able to build structure and process without waiting for someone else to define it.

Additional information:

Vacancy:

The salary range for this position is $110K-$135K
. Actual salary within the salary range will be based on a variety of factors including relevant experience, knowledge, and skills. A range of medical, dental, RRSP, paid time off, and/or other benefits also are available to all permanent employees.

Lambert Nemec Group, Winnipeg's leader in Permanent Accounting & Finance Recruitment, has partnered with our client, a high-growth, Winnipeg-based organization, to recruit a highly analytical and business-savvy Associate Vice-President, Financial Planning & Analysis
. The AVP of FP&A will be responsible for a broad range of responsibilities including but not limited to owning the annual business planning and budgeting cycle, building out forecasting and scenario modelling capabilities, developing performance dashboards and KPIs, and partnering closely with business unit leaders across the organization. This is an exceptional opportunity for a seasoned finance professional who thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and is looking for a role with strong visibility to senior leadership, given the exceptional cross-functional exposure this opportunity provides.

Responsibilities

The Associate Vice-President, Financial Planning & Analysis is responsible to:

Administer the annual budgeting cycle and maintain a regular cadence of in-year monthly forecasting.
Oversee financial planning processes and systems across the organization.
Partner with business unit leaders to build and maintain planning models, run scenario analyses, and prepare forecasts.
Analyze and report on financial and operational results to provide senior leadership with insight into business performance.
Develop and maintain dashboards and KPIs, including tracking of variances to plan and progress on cost-saving and revenue initiatives.
Communicate the drivers behind business unit performance and results directly to senior leadership.
Provide detailed analysis and commentary on results, partnering directly with departmental leaders on their numbers.
Evaluate historical budget and spending trends to inform future planning cycles.
Provide insight to senior leadership on financial modelling, forecasting, and profitability.

Requirements

Post-secondary education in accounting, finance, or a related field.
Canadian accounting designation, CPA (CA, CGA, CMA) or CFA required.
5+ years of progressive financial planning & analysis experience, or relevant analytical experience gained within a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
Experience working within a larger, multi-divisional organization.
Highly proficient in Excel and business intelligence tools, with experience across enterprise financial systems.
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with the ability to problem-solve complex issues.
Strong interpersonal and influencing skills, with the ability to communicate effectively and engage with people at all levels across the organization.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and written and verbal communication skills.
Comfortable in a fast-paced, evolving environment with a high tolerance for ambiguity and the ability to manage a large volume of competing priorities.
This is a fully in-office opportunity

Rewards

Opportunity provides exceptional exposure and interaction with senior Finance leadership and cross-functional stakeholders across the business.
Join an organization in an active, high-growth stage, with genuine long-term career growth potential as the finance team continues to scale.

Please complete our confidential online registration at www.lambertnemec.com to be considered for this opportunity or send your resume (in Word format) directly to Kyne Hunt, VP of Recruitment and Advisory at kyne@lambertnemec.com quoting Associate Vice-President, Financial Planning & Analysis in the subject.

ACAMS is the global leader in certification, training, and intelligence for anti-financial crime (AFC) professionals. ACAMS sets the standard for how organizations prevent, detect, and respond to money laundering, fraud and sanctions evasion. Trusted by 70% of the world's leading banks, as well as governmental and law enforcement agencies, and FinTechs, the organization has 120,000+ members across 200+ countries and territories. The Director of Digital owns the strategy, roadmap, and ongoing delivery of ACAMS.org and the broader ACAMS Digital Ecosystem. jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Reporting
jobs.description:
Most financial reporting functions are measured by whether deadlines are met. That’s important, but this role gets to decide what excellence looks like while meeting deadlines.

With accountability for external reporting and technical accounting, the Senior Director, Financial Reporting will play a defining role in advancing the reporting function of a Canadian-headquartered public manufacturing company. Reporting to the VP, Finance, this leader will oversee the full reporting cycle and strengthen the processes, controls, technical expertise and team required to support its continued evolution.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can deliver against current reporting requirements while strengthening the function for the future. The successful candidate will bring experience from a rigorous public company reporting environment and the judgment to apply that experience within a Finance organization that continues to evolve.

The Mandate

The Senior Director will have end-to-end responsibility for quarterly and annual public company reporting under IFRS, ensuring financial statements, disclosures and supporting documentation meet the standards required of a public company.

The role will also serve as a key technical accounting resource across Finance, providing guidance on complex and non-routine matters and ensuring accounting positions are well considered, documented and communicated.

Key responsibilities include:
Lead quarterly and annual public company reporting, including the preparation and review of external financial statements and disclosures under IFRS.
Own the reporting process from planning through review and completion, with clear accountability for quality, accuracy and timelines.
Provide technical accounting leadership across Finance, interpreting and applying IFRS to complex and judgmental matters.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos covering areas such as goodwill, impairment and significant accounting estimates.
Support potential US GAAP considerations and the requirements associated with a potential conversion.
Provide accounting support for M&A transactions, integrations and divestitures as they arise.
Lead reporting and technical accounting discussions with external auditors, ensuring issues are properly analyzed, documented and resolved.
Strengthen reporting processes, controls, documentation and review standards.
Identify opportunities to create greater consistency, efficiency and discipline across the reporting function.
Lead, coach and develop the team, including a planned Senior Manager, Technical Accounting hire.
Partner closely with Finance and Tax on accounting and reporting matters.
Build effective relationships with senior leaders and C-suite stakeholders, communicating complex issues clearly and credibly.

What You Bring

You are a CPA/CA with progressive public company financial reporting experience and strong technical accounting capability. You understand the discipline required in a public company environment and have experience taking ownership of a reporting process from beginning to end.

Your background includes:
CPA/CA designation, ideally with a foundation in public accounting.
Progressive public company financial reporting experience with direct ownership of quarterly and annual reporting.
Strong IFRS technical accounting expertise and experience applying guidance to complex accounting matters.
Experience preparing and reviewing technical accounting memos on significant, judgmental and non-routine issues.
The technical depth and judgment required to support potential US GAAP conversion requirements.
Experience working directly with external auditors and supporting accounting positions through clear analysis and documentation.
M&A-related accounting experience, including exposure to integrations and divestitures, considered a strong asset.
A track record of improving reporting processes, controls and standards.
Proven people leadership experience, including coaching, development and performance management.
Comfort working in a fast-paced environment where processes and capabilities continue to be refined.

How You Lead

You bring the technical credibility to navigate complex accounting matters and the business judgment to understand their broader implications. You are comfortable operating in the detail, but you know when to step back, engage others and move an issue toward resolution.

Your leadership is reflected in how you:
Establish and maintain a high standard for reporting quality.
Apply sound judgment when accounting guidance requires thoughtful interpretation.
Communicate complex matters clearly to audiences with varying levels of technical knowledge.
Build trusted relationships across the reporting team, Finance, Tax, external auditors and the C-suite.
Create accountability through clear expectations, ongoing feedback and meaningful coaching.
Develop people while addressing performance concerns directly and fairly.

The Opportunity

For someone who has developed their experience in a strong public company reporting environment, this role provides the opportunity to take on a broader leadership mandate within a manufacturing business headquartered in Canada.

The Senior Director will have the scope to improve how the reporting function operates, strengthen its technical accounting capability, develop the team and introduce the structure needed to support the organization as it evolves.

It is a role for a financial reporting leader who enjoys the rigor of public company reporting but also wants the opportunity to build, improve and leave the function stronger.

Apply in confidence.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

As a Turner & Townsend Project Management Director, you’ll be responsible for client management and department-related management services within multiple geographic markets, programs, and asset classes to achieve the company's strategic business objectives by delivering outstanding results to our client.

This job is part of the Enterprise Project Management division. They are responsible for the management of projects from initiation through completion for dedicated client groups as part of a multi-service outsourcing contract. You will be responsible for global teams delivering commercial office fit-out, retail and Move Adds & Change services.

Who are you?

You are an expert Real Estate
Project Management Director
with a minimum of 12+
years post-graduate experience
in real estate project management
looking for the next step or are currently undertaking a similar role in a similar environment.

Job Description

Communicate with the client and manage client expectations on resourcing needs, project and programme performance, risks, status reporting, and issues escalation
Direct all phases of the delivery process for large and high-profile clients including procurement, contracting, planning, tracking, and execution
Provide formal supervision to direct report employees in Canada, the US and EMEA. Monitor the training and development of staff. Conduct performance evaluations and coaching. Oversee the recruiting and hiring of new employees.
Coordinate and manage the team's daily activities. Establish work schedules, assign tasks, and cross-train staff. Set and track staff and department deadlines. Mentor and coach as needed.
Ensure that contract procurement, negotiation, execution, administration, and closeouts are accurate, timely, and compliant.
Develop new business growth and maintain existing business relationships.
Maintain full responsibility for the financial performance of market, program, and client accounts.
Identify complex project risks, lead reviews, and develop risk mitigation and backup plans.
Apply deep knowledge of multiple disciplines, broad industry knowledge, and commercial awareness. Drive financial and functional performance within disciplines and across business.
Lead by example and model behaviors that are consistent with Turner & Townsend values. Negotiate with senior management, customers, and external parties of divergent interests to reach an agreement of strategic importance while being guided by the business segment and the organization's functional strategy.
Conceptualize new methods, techniques, processes, and standards across job disciplines or functions.
Direct the resolution of highly complex or unusual business problems by applying advanced critical thinking.
Work in partnership with the Account Alliance Director, Facility Management teams, Transaction teams, Procurement and other teams to provide a fully integrated and seamless service.
Ensure that all account KPI’s and SLA’s are achieved.

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree preferred with 12-15 years of relevant real estate project delivery experience. In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education will be considered. LEED AP, PMP, and/or CCM designation(s) preferred.
Polished communicator with experience presenting and liaising with client executive and C-Suite level employees.
In-depth knowledge of financial terms and principles and the ability to analyze the most complex business/financial data and develop innovative solutions.
Experience in the areas of staffing, selection, training, development, coaching, mentoring, measuring, appraising, and rewarding performance and retention is preferred.
Ability to exchange sensitive, complicated, and difficult information, convey performance expectations and handle problems.
Leadership skills to motivate the team to achieve broad operational targets with impacts on own job discipline, multiple job disciplines, and department.
In-depth knowledge of Microsoft Office products. Examples include Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.
Expert organizational skills with an unrivaled inquisitive mindset.
Ideally you have retail
project delivery experience and experience with clients/organizations in the financial and professional services sector.

Additional Information

What's in it for you...

100% covered health and dental benefits for you and your dependents (including paramedical services)
Health spending account, to top up expenses not covered in the benefits program
RRSP option with company matching
Annual learning and development budget
Access to a range of online learning tools, and support for career development and growth
Coverage of one professional membership or license fee per year, if directly related to your role

jobs.title: Senior Director, Clinical Development Change & Transformation Lead
jobs.description:
Evinova is a health-tech business within the AstraZeneca Group, created to accelerate better health outcomes by driving digital transformation across the life sciences sector. We bring together science-based expertise, evidence-led rigor, and deep human insight to design digital solutions that help healthcare work better for everyone. Operating at the intersection of healthcare, technology, data, and analytics, we are changing how clinical research is conducted, how care is delivered, and how patients experience it, with solutions built to scale and to deliver better outcomes for patients worldwide.

We are driven by a shared purpose: to transform health through data and digital innovation. Our teams collaborate across disciplines to solve complex problems, continuously learning and evolving in a fast-paced, high-impact environment.

We are seeking a Director, Clinical Development Change & Transformation Lead to drive the change management and adoption work that turns Evinova's solutions into new ways of working across clinical development. Working within the transformation strategy and roadmap set by Evinova's Clinical Development Digital Innovation & Transformation leadership, you will lead the day-to-day delivery: redesigning processes with functional owners, preparing and equipping the workforce for change, and building the working relationships with Therapeutic Areas and Clinical Operations that turn deployment into real adoption and captured benefit.

You will be a visible, trusted presence on the ground in Mississauga — understanding the stakeholder landscape, running rollout and readiness activities, keeping communication and governance cadences moving, and channelling frontline insight and new ideas back to our product teams. As our solutions mature, you will help turn what works into repeatable playbooks and deliverables that support external customers on their own change journeys.

This is a hands-on leadership role for an experienced change practitioner who combines clinical development fluency with practical transformation delivery — organized, independent amid ambiguity, credible with senior customers, and energized by turning bold technology into real-world change.

Responsibilities

Change & Adoption Delivery: Lead the delivery of change management and adoption plans for Evinova's AI-enabled solutions across clinical development, translating the transformation strategy and roadmap into actionable workstream plans, turning points, and deliverables.

Stakeholder Engagement & Relationships:
Build and maintain working relationships across Therapeutic Areas, Clinical Operations, and enabling functions (e.g., Biometrics, Regulatory, Medical Writing, Quality). Maintain the stakeholder landscape map, act as a day-to-day point of contact for adoption, and prepare and support senior-level engagement where needed.

Process Redesign:
Lead process redesign workshops with functional and process owners: document current-state workflows, co-design AI-enabled future-state ways of working, and drive the actions needed to transition, including inputs to the controlled procedure and training updates that a regulated environment requires.

Workforce Readiness & Capability Building:
Deliver role and skills impact assessments, develop and run training and upskilling programs, and help embed responsible, compliant use of AI into daily work.

Rollout Execution:
Manage rollout execution in partnership with Product, Delivery, and customer teams — wave plans, readiness assessments, training logistics, hypercare, and post-launch support — and track issues and risks through to closure.

Communications & Governance:
Develop and run communication plans and engagement cadences across functions and sites, prepare executive updates and governance materials, and facilitate working groups and change forums.

Adoption Measurement & Benefits Tracking:
Track adoption and value measures — utilization, cycle-time and effort reduction, time-to-value, and user satisfaction — build the associated reporting and dashboards, and contribute to benefits validation with Finance against the argument.

Feedback Channels & Product Input: Run structured feedback channels — user advisory groups, voice-of-customer sessions, and adoption analytics — synthesize insight into prioritized recommendations and new ideas for Product, and support pilots and user validation of improvements before scaling.

Playbooks & External Customer Support: Contribute to and maintain transformation playbooks, toolkits, and deliverables, and support Commercial and Delivery teams in deploying them with external sponsors and CROs on their change journeys.

Change Champion Network: Build and coach the change champion and practitioner network across the portfolio, and lead the matrixed or small-team resources assigned to change workstreams [confirm team scope with Talent Acquisition].

Qualifications

Required (Must-Have)

Significant experience delivering change management, transformation, or technology adoption programs within pharmaceutical R&D, biotech, or health technology.
Strong understanding of clinical development and Clinical Operations processes, roles, and pain points — from protocol design through study conduct and close-out.
Hands-on experience implementing AI or digital solutions into ways of working, including impact assessments, process redesign, and training and capability building.
Strong stakeholder management: credibility with Director- and Senior Director-level stakeholders and the ability to influence across a matrixed, global organization.
Practical process redesign and facilitation skills (e.g., Lean, design thinking, or service design methodologies), with the ability to run workshops and produce clear current-state and future-state deliverables.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to craft change narratives, training content, and executive-ready updates.
Experience running feedback mechanisms and translating user insight into actionable recommendations.
Comfort defining and tracking adoption metrics and benefits, including building reporting and dashboards.
Organized, independent delivery: able to manage multiple workstreams amid ambiguity and competing priorities and drive issues to resolution.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree a plus.

Additional Qualifications

Experience within a SaaS, product-led, or digital health organization.
Formal change management certification (e.g., Prosci/ADKAR, ACMP CCMP).
Familiarity with GxP-regulated environments and clinical trial technologies (study design platforms, eCOA, RBQM, and monitoring solutions).
Experience supporting generative or agentic AI deployments in an enterprise setting.
Experience building and leading change champion networks or communities of practice.
Experience in customer-facing roles across sponsor, CRO, or vendor environments.

SO, WHAT’S NEXT?

To be considered for this exciting opportunity, please complete the full application on our website at your earliest convenience – it is the only way that our Recruiter and Hiring Manager can know that you feel well qualified for this opportunity. If you know someone who would be a great fit, please share this posting with them.

Where can I find out more?

Explore what we’re building: www.evinova.com
Stay connected and see our impact in action: https://www.linkedin.com/company/evinova/

Apply today to bring smarter, faster clinical trials to life!

jobs.title: Senior Director Finance
jobs.description:
Senior Director, Finance Help build Canada's next global success story.

We are hiring for one of Canada's fastest growing technology companies, recognized by Deloitte as the #1 Enterprise Software company in the 2025 North American Technology Fast 500 and ranked #5 in Deloitte Canada's 2024 Technology Fast 50 Companies to Watch.

This is a rare opportunity for an accomplished finance leader to join a high growth Canadian technology company at a pivotal stage of its journey, with a clear path toward a future VP.

We are looking for someone who has been there before. A leader who has helped companies scale, built teams and financial infrastructure, navigated complexity and knows how to evolve a finance function as a business moves into its next chapter.

You will work closely with the CFO, CEO, and colleagues across the leadership team in a highly collaborative environment where finance is a strategic partner to the business.
This is an opportunity to help shape what comes next.

The Mandate

As Director, Finance, you will build and evolve the finance function to support continued growth across Canada, the US, UK and Australia.

Your mandate will include:

Build and lead a finance function and team designed for scale
Strengthen financial controls, governance, reporting and infrastructure
Lead controllership, accounting operations and financial reporting
Develop robust budgeting, forecasting and long-range planning capabilities
Partner with executive and operational leaders to drive visibility into performance, margins and business opportunities
Turn financial and operational data into insights that improve decision-making
Lead cash flow, treasury and capital planning
Support board reporting, investor communications and strategic planning
Drive improvements across finance systems, billing and processes
Partner with leadership on new markets, products, partnerships and other growth opportunities

Who You Are

You are an experienced finance leader who knows what it takes to scale a business.
You have likely been part of a company going through significant growth and understand that the finance function has to evolve alongside it.
You know how to build the team, systems and processes needed for the next stage without creating unnecessary complexity or slowing the business down.

You bring:

Significant finance leadership experience in a high-growth technology, SaaS, platform or technology-enabled business
A proven track record of scaling companies and building high-performing teams
Strong experience across controllership, FP&A, strategic finance and business partnering
Experience working directly with CEOs, CFOs and executive leadership teams
Strong commercial judgment and the ability to connect finance to business performance
The ability to operate strategically while remaining close enough to the business to get things done
A collaborative, low-ego leadership style and the confidence to influence across functions
Experience thriving in entrepreneurial, fast-moving environments
CPA, CA or equivalent professional qualification

Why This Role

You will join at a moment when the company has significant momentum and an even bigger ambition.

You will have the opportunity to build, influence and grow alongside the business, working with an executive team that values collaboration, ownership and people who know how to turn ambition into execution.

For the right leader, this role is more than the next step in finance.

It is the opportunity to help shape the finance function, build a team, influence the direction of the company and grow into a broader VP level mandate as the business scales.

If you've helped build companies before and are ready to help build what comes next, this could be the opportunity you've been waiting for.

Build something extraordinary. Build something Canada can be proud of.

new_jobs.title: Director of Digital
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are:

ACAMS is the global leader in certification, training, and intelligence for anti-financial crime (AFC) professionals. ACAMS sets the standard for how organizations prevent, detect, and respond to money laundering, fraud and sanctions evasion. Trusted by 70% of the world's leading banks, as well as governmental and law enforcement agencies, and FinTechs, the organization has 120,000+ members across 200+ countries and territories. Its 65+ chapters and annual conferences connect AFC professionals across every major financial center. Learn more at acams.org.

Opportunity at a Glance

The Director of Digital owns the strategy, roadmap, and ongoing delivery of ACAMS.org and the broader ACAMS Digital Ecosystem. This is more than a website leadership role: our digital platform is a product in its own right, spanning discovery, trial, purchase, and renewal of certifications, training, membership, and subscription-based news and intelligence content. You will act as the connective tissue between Marketing, Product, Sales, Operations, and News/Intelligence — translating business goals into a prioritized backlog and shipping continuously through an agile delivery process.

Responsibilities

Develop and maintain the roadmap for ACAMS.org, with stakeholder buy-in, spanning the full Digital Lifecycle: Find, Try, Buy, Renew, and Consume
Play a leading role in defining the product vision for the ACAMS Digital Ecosystem — an end-to-end digital experience supporting ACAMS members across their professional journeys, from first certification through ongoing intelligence and community engagement
Drive stakeholder alignment across Marketing, Product, Sales, Operations, and News/Intelligence divisions to maintain a unified backlog and prioritize website changes against business impact
Own the ongoing release of website enhancements and bug fixes through an agile delivery process, partnering with engineering, design, and vendor teams on sprint planning, QA, and launch
Optimize the digital commerce and subscription experience — conversion, self-service, and renewal — for products including premium news and intelligence content
Define and track KPIs for digital performance (traffic, conversion, engagement, retention) and use data and user research to inform prioritization
Lead and participate in regular executive updates on roadmap progress, results, and risks

Qualifications

8–10+ years in digital product management, digital experience, or e-commerce leadership, including ownership of a revenue-generating website or digital platform
Proven success managing a cross-functional backlog and shipping through agile processes (Scrum/Kanban) with internal teams and external partners
Experience with subscription, membership, or premium content business models; familiarity with CMS, e-commerce, CRM, and analytics platforms
Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills — able to build consensus across divisions with competing priorities
Data-driven decision-maker comfortable with web analytics, A/B testing, and customer journey optimization
Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or product management certification a plus. Familiarity with professional associations, credentialing, or B2B publishing environments is a strong plus

EEO

We are proud to be an EEO employer M/F/D/V. At ACAMS, we welcome everyone and have a strong commitment towards diversity and inclusion. We encourage our Colleagues to be their true authentic selves and support laws that prohibit discrimination everywhere we do business. We also maintain a drug-free workplace.
